citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google, Yale University)
description: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval) is a benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models. It focuses on a set of 25 types of "verifiable instructions" (e.g., "write in more than 400 words", "mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times") and consists of around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions that can be objectively checked with deterministic programs.
name: IFEval
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verification of instruction-following is performed using deterministic programs. A strict metric checks exact compliance; a loose metric applies transformations (removing markdown font modifiers, removing first/last lines, and combinations thereof — 8 total transformations) to reduce false negatives.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically — there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The loose accuracy metric was introduced to mitigate false negatives from naive string matching, though it may introduce false positives.
rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: (1) generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts; (3) applying few-shot prompting to rephrase each prompt for diversity; and (4) manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt, prior to filtering and rephrasing.
rai:dataLimitations: The current implementation has limited diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions, does not support multi-modal use cases, and the loose verification criterion may introduce false positives while the strict criterion may produce false negatives.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts; another few-shot prompting pass rephrased each prompt to increase phrasing diversity; finally, all rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited one by one.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to improve the safety and reliability of LLMs by providing an objective, reproducible evaluation of instruction-following ability, which is critical in high-stakes scenarios such as healthcare or autonomous systems.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using verifiable instructions that can be checked automatically and objectively.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting (using LLMs) was used to identify illogical prompts and to rephrase prompts for diversity during dataset construction.

These verifiable instructions are atomic instructions for which one can use a simple, interpretable, and deterministic program to verify if corresponding responses follow the instructions or not.

evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial, not only for the precision of tasks but also for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
